method.wave: wave = 1 + max(wave of deps in the SAME phase); deps on earlier phases are treated as satisfied (as docs/architecture/p1.md does for P1). globalWave uses all deps across phases. Conditional deps ("when the X cut is taken; otherwise ...") use the no-cut (default) list; the cut list is kept in depsIfCut.
method.criticalPath: Longest path by summed task hours through the dependency DAG (per phase: intra-phase deps; core/all: all deps, cross-phase).
method.parallelKind: serial = alone in its wave; claude-alongside-me = wave has both CLAUDE and ME/PAIR tasks, so they truly run concurrently; idle-wait-overlap = wave contains a long run (overnight, quota-bound, 48 h) so one person can do the other task while it runs; independent-serialize-for-one-person = DAG-independent but needs a human on each, so one person does them back to back.
method.idleWaitHeuristic: type==eval and title/acceptance mention overnight, 48 hours, split across days, bulk generation, or a Run ... ablation/phase run; or any task text saying overnight/48 hours. Heuristic, not hand-labelled.
method.meOnly: owner==ME. PLAN.md:18 / PROJECT.md:38 say [ME] owns the agent loop, tool schemas, context manager, verifier, judge rubric and calibration, eval scorer, workflow state machine, threat model and all ADRs; meKind splits ME tasks into reading-notes, adr, break-it, eval-run, core-build.

A call that would exceed a provider's measured daily limit is refused by the quota ledger before any HTTP request is sent (unit test).
`docs/quotas.md` holds the measured free-tier limits per provider and role, each with a date and a method.

phases.name: verify
phases.goal: Decide whether a patch really fixed the bug and broke nothing else, using deterministic checks first and a calibrated cross-family vision judge second. The judge does not override a passed check run. Best-of-k stays inside the P4-T19 selector, then the phase measures what best-of-k buys.
doneWhen: Four deterministic checks (pixel diff, overflow, axe, console) each pass on a clean tree and fail on a tree broken in the matching way, shown by one test per check.
A verifier pipeline runs the checks in a fixed order, short-circuits on the first hard failure and returns one structured verdict.
A 100-pair calibration set (ticket, before, after, your human label) exists, labelled by you.

Krippendorff's α between the judge and your labels is at least 0.80 on that set, with a bootstrap interval, and the order-disagreement rate is reported beside α. A disagreeing pair is not averaged into one label, and an unparsed judge string stays in the α denominator as `error`. If α is not reached within the T14 budget, ADR-013 records the shortfall and the judge is advisory only; that is a written decision, not a silent one. The judge does not override a passed check run.
The same-family and cross-family judges are both run on the calibration set, and best-of-k with k = 1, 3, 5 is run on the 30-task subset (Ablation table filled).
Phase report filled against P3.

criticalPath.reading: Critical path is the infinite-parallelism lower bound. One person at 20 h/week is bound by total hours, not the path; the path says which tasks cannot start until others finish and how much work is dependency-free.

weekly.ruleFromTasksMd: TASKS.md:3: weeks are 20 h bins; a week can run up to 3 h over because a task is placed in the week it starts; buffer weeks are 17 and 25 (after P4 and P6).

repackCheck.rule: week = floor(cumulative start hours / 20) + 1, shifted +1 after each buffer week
